decision: Positioning line locked: A multi-sensory cinematic literary experience unfolding in real time over six weeks.
reasoning: Line uses aspirational framing (cinematic, literary, multi-sensory) rather than oppositional — directly embodies the aspirational positioning thesis

Cross-reference research documented $1.55B in failed library-model platforms (Radish, Wattpad, Kindle Vella) and identified Quinn's premium curated model as the sole survivor — directly reinforcing the graveyard thesis. Kill test built on the premise that iteration sophistication is the moat, not volume.

Label strategy doc builds the full Indivizibel brand architecture — catalogue numbering, multi-format publishing, physical objects as catalogue items. Directly operationalizes the A24 label thesis with legal entity, trademark prosecution, and phased timeline.

Label strategy explicitly opens with 'Every failed serialized fiction venture — Quibi, Radish, Kindle Vella — made the same mistakes' and positions Indivizibel as premium, story-first, no micropayments.
Label strategy commits to $49/reader pricing throughout — revenue model, kill tests, and principles all built on experience pricing, not content pricing.

DayPublish module and editor manual are pure tooling — Claude built the export pipeline, backup system, and instruction docs without writing a single word of prose. The entire feature exists to help the author write; it generates no creative content.

Revenue waterfall math is built entirely on $49 experience pricing — return tables, investor payback timeline, and hockey stick projections all depend on experience-tier pricing rather than content pricing. Ignition cohort strategy validates $49 with hand-picked readers.

The 2-year thesis test with kill gate is structured as the inverse of the graveyard companies — premium single title proving unit economics before scaling, vs. library model burning capital on content volume. The $292K raise is explicitly positioned against the $1.55B graveyard.

Tranched funding strategy, Hannah/Seb compensation, and overage scenarios all built on $49 experience pricing. Investor return math, revenue waterfall, and the argument against $875K all depend on experience-tier pricing.

Refusing to inflate budget to $875K despite available capital directly mirrors anti-graveyard discipline — prove unit economics with minimum capital before scaling, the opposite of Radish/Wattpad/Vella burning capital on volume.
